The length of a spring when no force acts on it is $L$. The spring constant of the spring is $3.0 \times 10^3 \text{ Nm}^{-1}$.
The spring is on the floor of an accelerating lift (elevator), and the spring supports a $30 \text{ kg}$ mass.
The lift is accelerating downwards at $2.0 \text{ ms}^{-2}$.
What is the difference between $L$ and the length of the spring when the lift is accelerating downwards?
(gravitational field strength $= 10 \text{ Nkg}^{-1}$; the spring obeys Hooke's law)
